canonical_data: per-session working directories holding agent logs, trace records, plan files and JSON memory summaries, plus a component version registry saved to JSON
current_repo_note: The GitHub description still calls it a hierarchical multi-agent system for deep research, but the README now calls it "a self-evolution protocol and runtime" and the default tool-calling config leaves the deep_researcher tool commented out. Vendored LightRAG sources carry no licence file in the tree, and two SIL Open Font License notices sit beside fonts in an optional visualizer asset folder; neither changes the root MIT grant.
strengths: One registry-and-config pattern covers agents, tools, environments, memory systems and optimizers, and the shipped configs wire a planner and tool-calling sub-agents together over a message bus
A reflection, TextGrad, GRPO and Reinforce++ optimizer set lets an agent's prompts be revised from recorded trajectories, with a tracer and a component version manager kept alongside
The tool-calling agent runs a bounded step loop (50 steps in the shipped config) over bash, Python, file, web, todo and skill-generator tools plus an MCP importer
weaknesses: The README's protocol claims are not backed by code: the names RSPL and SEPL appear only in the two README files, and the version manager registers, deprecates and archives versions but has no rollback function despite the stated "auditable lineage and rollback"
The bash tool starts commands with a shell subprocess on the host with only a 30-second timeout, and the tool-calling agent contains no approval or confirmation step
Dormant since 2026-05-04 with two tags, one documented run command and a project homepage that returns 404, so adoption evidence is thin for a repository with thousands of stars
why_it_matters: A readable example of an agent stack that couples tool-calling agents with trajectory-driven prompt optimization, and a caution that its README describes more protocol than the code implements.
